toxicity.Notes: Acute toxicity study, section 3.4: the nickel(II) complex showed toxicity at 55 mg/kg body weight and caused mortality in mice within 24 h, with little behavioural change and no difference in food or water intake. Behaviour was watched for the first 3 h and then every 4 h over 24 h, which is the only observation period stated. The abstract calls 55 mg/kg the LD50 of the complex and that is the number recorded here, but the Results describe it only as the dose that killed the animals: no dose series, no mortality count, no calculation method and no group size are given, so those fields stay empty. The route conflicts between the two places in the paper: section 2.7 calls the experiment an acute oral toxicity study, while section 3.4 writes 55 mg/kg (i.p.); i.p. is recorded because it is the route given with the number itself and the route used throughout the EAC work. The strain and animal details are from section 2.6, Swiss Webster mice of 6-8 weeks and 25 +/- 4 g, housed six per cage; the sex is male for the toxicity study. The antitumour work in the same paper is an Ehrlich ascites carcinoma model scored as percentage inhibition of EAC cell growth, 28.21 % for the ligand and 44.52 % for the complex at 0.3 mg/kg/day i.p. for five days and 69.36 % for the complex at 2.75 mg/kg/day, with bleomycin at 0.3 mg/kg/day as the standard. That endpoint is a cell count in ascitic fluid, not tumour growth inhibition, so no main row is created. Treatment arm (column removed 2026-11-09): [Ni(HL)CH3CN], single i.p. dose, acute toxicity study. Cohort (column removed 2026-11-09): aoc4601-ld50.
